description_en: Group of four damaged stone statues kept at a Śiva temple.This record concerns only three stone statues kept at a Śiva temple. The temple is found on the northern side of the road coming from Khalaṅgā and going to Tallo Khalaṅgā. The site is located on the western end of Amargaḍhi and east of the Tundikhel ground.The statues are all damaged. The objects may date from circa 17th-19th century. They are very similar to some of the statues found in the subsidiary temples of Ugratārā Mandira, located some 10 km north-east. One possibility to explain the state of the images would be that they were produced at the same time as the ones from Ugratārā Mandira, and came from the same workshop. They may have been damaged during violent events such as one of the battles between the Doṭeli king Hariśāhī II (17th-18th century) and the Mughals or the Kumaonis (events briefly mentioned inPandey 1997: 179-180). The taking of the kingdom of Doṭi around 1790, under general Amar Singh Thapa, of which Dadeldhura was a part during the 18th century, may be another moment where the statues would have been damaged. Nevertheless, the battles for the conquest of Doṭi were mainly fought elsewhere.Another explanation could be that the statues are rejects from a local workshop.The statues represent a Mother Goddess, probably Hārītī (001, 37 x 27 x 9 cm), a fragment of a four handed deity (002, 17 x 16 x 5 cm) and a standing character next to a quadruped (003, 24 x 22 x 7 cm). The latter may represent the goddess Durgā with a lion or tiger.
monument_assessment: Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages)
references: REFERENCES Pandey, R. N. 1997. Making of Modern Nepal. A study of History, Art and Culture of the Principalities of Western Nepal . New Delhi: Nirala Publications.
